subject: Redwood network isolation & threat-model summary for Crestline RFP
messages:
From: Alex Hunter <alex.hunter@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@crestlinehealth.com
Date: 2026-06-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: network isolation + threat-model artifacts request

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this RFP. As part of our vendor security review we need a concise packet that covers:
- your network isolation model between tenant workloads and control plane
- ingress/egress filtering and public endpoint exposure
- key management and KMS/HSM boundaries
- a brief threat model summary (high-level risks + mitigations)

Can you attach a network diagram and a short narrative (1-2 pages) suitable for our security committee? We have a deadline next Friday 2026-06-18 for initial packet review.

Also include any audit artifacts (SOC2 or relevant attestations) or links to where those can be retrieved. If you prefer, we can schedule a 45 minute technical deep dive next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Hunter
Director, Procurement
Crestline Health
[external attachment: crestline_RFP_qs.xlsx (Excel, 45 KB)]
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hunter <alex.hunter@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: network isolation + threat-model artifacts request

Alex —

Appreciate the clear list. Attaching a compact packet that should hit the items you requested: network diagram, isolation model summary, and a high-level threat model. See attachments.

Highlights (TL;DR):
- Isolation: customer workloads run in tenant-scoped execution pools with per-tenant vNets and strict egress ACLs; control plane is separated into a private management VPC with no direct tenant routing.
- Network flows: all tenant ingress is fronted by customer-configurable edge endpoints (TLS, mTLS options) and sits behind model-serving gateways; default egress is blocked unless explicitly allowed via managed egress rules.
- KMS/HSM: customer keys can be brought via KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or on-prem HSM via PKCS#11). Secrets are never stored in plaintext and rotate with configurable policies.
- Threat model summary: prioritized risks (data exfiltration, lateral movement, model poisoning) and mitigations (KV cache scoping, signed model artifacts, runtime attestation, incremental rollouts + canary runway).

Attachments (stubs included):
- redwood_network_isolation_summary_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB) — diagram + explanatory notes
- rfi_responses_table.csv (CSV, 12 KB) — row-aligned answers to your spreadsheet

We can also provide a redacted runtime threat-model notes doc if useful — Karthik has the latest.

Would you like to set the technical deep dive for next Wednesday 2026-06-16 at 10:00 AM PT? I can invite the infra leads.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: FW: RFP: network isolation + threat-model artifacts request (internal technical notes)

Naomi / Marissa —

Putting internal notes here for the packet and the deep dive. Keep this internal — do not forward the full doc externally without redaction. Key points to include in the meeting and the one-page threat summary:

1) Runtime Isolation Model (concise bullets for external doc):
   - Multi-tenant scheduler with soft isolation via cgroups + strict KV cache namespace enforcement.
   - Hardware-level isolation option: dedicated GPU pools (Dedicated offering) for customers requiring physical tenancy.
   - Network: per-tenant subnetting, egress gateway with allowlist, and optional private link / VPC peering for private deployments.

2) Threat mitigations we should explicitly call out:
   - KV cache scoping: per-tenant keys + TTL-based purges; cross-tenant cache poisoning risk mitigated by signed prefixes and cache validation hooks.
   - Model artifact verification: signed model bundles verified at load time; rollback on checksum mismatch.
   - Secure bootstrapping: attestation for new nodes joining the pool; only approved kernel images via image-signing.

3) Audit & evidence pointers to surface:
   - SOC2 Type II report (redacted) via our compliance portal (link in the Drive packet).
   - Network firewall rule samples + sample VPC peering config (sanitized).

4) Suggested answers to Crestline's likely follow-ups:
   - "Can we bring our own HSM?" — Yes; we support PKCS#11 integrations and isolated key stores on Dedicated and Private tiers.
   - "What happens during a node compromise?" — We isolate the node, evict workloads, rotate affected keys, and failover to warm capacity; details in incident response appendix.

Attachments (internal only): redwood_runtime_threat_model_notes.docx (DOCX, 230 KB).

I'll prepare the slide for the threat-model page and drop it into the shared drive link. Naomi — if you confirm the deep dive time, I'll be on the call to walk the diagram and the attack surfaces.

- Karthik
Principal Infra Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
[karthik internal attachment: redwood_runtime_threat_model_notes.docx (DOCX, 230 KB)]
From: Alex Hunter <alex.hunter@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@crestlinehealth.com
Date: 2026-06-12T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: network isolation + threat-model artifacts request

Naomi —

Thanks for the prompt turnaround and the packet. The network diagram was helpful. A few quick clarifications from our security committee after initial review:

1) Can you provide an example of the firewall rule set you push to tenant egress gateways (sanitized)?
2) For customers using the Hosted API with regional deployments, is traffic between customer region and control plane encrypted in transit and restricted to private peering when requested?
3) We need confirmation that cross-tenant logs are never accessible across tenant accounts; is that enforced at storage policy level?

Also, our legal wants to confirm whether SOC2 artifacts can be shared under NDA; procurement will send an NDA and a short DocuSign link. If possible, please add a brief appendix that lists the versions of major controls (e.g., TLS min version, KMS providers supported).

If you can respond to those three items by end of day Monday 2026-06-15, we can proceed to scheduling the deep dive.

Regards,
Alex
